item.title: Journeys to Resilience
item.description: The article examines the phenomenon of “prepping” from the perspective of conversion research. Based on a qualitative content analysis of postings from a big prepper online forum in the U.S., it explores the causes and modalities of adopting prepping as a lifestyle. The causes include biographical instances, experiences of disaster and emergency, reports from others and a general sense of threat. item.title: Stony Knowledge
item.description: The use of precious stones for magical, apotropaic, and medical purposes has been well-documented since Antiquity. item.title: History Carved on a Tombstone
item.description: This paper aims to edit and analyse an unpublished Arabic tombstone from the Ibn ʿAbbās public cemetery in Ṭāʾif. It also explores a related historical theme, i.e., the continuity of the descendants of an Arab poet down to the twelfth century. This tombstone contains the name of a deceased individual, linked to Yazīd b. Miqsam al-Thaqafī, an influential poet from Ṭāʾif in the eighth century AD (second century AH). item.title: The Notion of ‘Effortlessness’ in the Dzogchen Commentaries by Nubchen Sangye Yeshe
item.description: The present contribution will seek to explore the notion of effortlessness in the Dzogchen commentaries by Nubchen Sangye Yeshe (ca. 844–mid-tenth century), examining its role as a key theme in the self-understanding of the emergent Dzogchen tradition’s approach to contemplative practice. item.title: “Nothing to Be Practiced” (bsgom du med)
item.description: The term ‘nothing to be practiced’ often appears in the instruction genres of the Tibetan Kagyupa tradition. item.title: The Way to the Way: Classical Daoist Apophatic Meditation as Effortless Practice
item.description: The present article explores Daoist effortless meditation with particular attention to its association with the inner cultivation lineages of classical Daoism (ca. 350–ca. 90 BCE).
